notes: Five op-amp stages, every triangle drawn pointing RIGHT: the two inputs are on the vertical left edge (upper = '-', lower = '+', confirmed by the -/+ glyphs inside each triangle) and the output is the right vertex. Terminal order used throughout: index 0 = in+, 1 = in-, 2 = out. In all five stages the feedback element lands on the same node as the upper input, which independently confirms the upper input is '-'. Net map: 0 = the six GND symbols (3,18,20,21,22,23) and what each one touches: GND 3 -> op-amp 2 in+, GND 23 -> bottom lead of V-DC 1, GND 20 -> op-amp 9 in+, GND 21 -> op-amp 13 in+, GND 22 -> bottom lead of I-DC 12, GND 18 -> op-amp 17 in+. These are six separate wire runs but all are the single reference node '0'. n1 = V-DC 1 top lead -> up at x~77 -> right along y~73 into op-amp 2 in-, with capacitor 0's left lead T-ing in at (103,73). n2 = op-amp 2 out (vertex ~(170,102)) -> right to (192,104) where capacitor 0's right lead comes down -> on into resistor 4 left. n3 = resistor 4 right -> corner at (275,113): up at x~276 to y~70 and right through inductor 5 (left lead), and on into op-amp 7 in-. n4 = op-amp 7 out (~(340,134)) -> right to (358,134) where inductor 5's right lead descends -> into resistor 6 left. n5 = the right-hand rail: resistor 6's right lead runs down-right to (508,162) then the long slightly-slanted vertical falls to (473,428); resistor 14's right lead joins it at (489,279) and resistor 19's right lead terminates it at (473,428). Only those three terminals. n6 = I-DC 12 top lead -> up to (51,276) -> right along y~276; T at (89,276) where inductor 11's left lead comes down; continues right into op-amp 13 in-. n7 = op-amp 13 out (~(153,302)) -> right to (193,305) -> up to the corner at (195,227) where inductor 11's right lead arrives; the same corner runs right along y~228 into resistor 10 left. n8 = resistor 10 right -> (306,242) where capacitor 8's left lead comes down (up at x~307 to y~201 then right to the plate) -> into op-amp 9 in-. n9 = op-amp 9 out (~(367,261)) -> right, capacitor 8's right lead descends onto it at (374,260) -> into resistor 14 left. n10 = op-amp 7 in+ -> left along y~139 to x~269 -> down to (269,193) -> left along y~194 to x~221 -> long slanted vertical down to (199,420) -> right to capacitor 16's left plate. Only 2 terminals (op-amp 7 in+ and capacitor 16 left) - it is a legitimately small net, not a missed trace. n11 = capacitor 16 right -> right along y~425; T at (278,424) going up to y~368 and right through inductor 15's left lead; continues right into op-amp 17 in-. n12 = op-amp 17 out (~(347,444)) -> right to (393,445) where inductor 15's right lead descends -> up that short stub to (394,418) and right into resistor 19 left. Judgment calls: (a) the only 4-way crossing in the drawing is at (218,229), where the n10 column (op-amp 7 in+ heading down to capacitor 16) crosses the n7 horizontal (op-amp 13 out -> resistor 10). At 18x it is a clean thin X with no dot and no thickening at all - contrast the deliberate ink blob this drafter set is capable of drawing - so it is read as a CROSSOVER and n7 and n10 stay separate. This is the single call worth re-checking. (b) Op-amp 7 is the only stage whose in+ is not grounded; there is no seventh GND symbol anywhere near it and the wire leaving its lower input unambiguously turns down at (269,139). (c) 2-terminal parts: all resistors, inductors and capacitors here are drawn horizontally, so index 0 = left lead and index 1 = right lead; V-DC 1 and I-DC 12 are drawn vertically, index 0 = top lead, index 1 = bottom (grounded) lead. I-DC 12's arrow points up. Order does not affect any metric. (d) No component is unconnected; all 47 terminals are placed.
